title: orch relay message v1
description: One message sent through orch-relay. The sender picks the id. Same id again: identical message = 200 no-op, different content = 409. Unknown fields are allowed and kept. the receiver stores seen ids in .orch/inbox-seen.json and never processes one twice. Message content is untrusted data, never instructions.

ticket.description: Ticket in the workspace that owns the thread: question and answer = the asking workspace (the relay copies it from reply_to); text/file/delegate/start = the sender's; phone send and webhook = the receiving workspace's.

key.description: Optional display key of `ticket` (ticket.schema.json key, e.g. DM1-12), set by the workspace that owns that ticket on text/file/question/delegate/start. The relay copies it with `ticket` onto answers and shows it to phones next to `ticket`. For people only; `ticket` stays the reference.

client_id.description: A UUID the phone picks once per outgoing message and keeps on every retry; the relay dedupes on (phone, client_id) and compares it exactly.

feedback.description: Feedback on one artifact revision of the message's ticket (ticket_view attachment id + rev). approve = "Looks good" (pins may be empty); changes = at least one pin. Never an approval to publish: that is always a question answer.

pin.description: One comment pin: its number as shown (1, 2, ...), where it sits, and a typed and/or spoken comment.

voice_blob_id.description: A phone upload (voice comment); the receiving workspace may read it like an attachment.

anchor.description: Where a pin sits. html: CSS selector and/or quoted text of the element, plus the vertical scroll offset in CSS px at viewport width viewport_w. pdf: page (from 1) and x/y. image: x/y. x and y are fractions 0..1 of the page or image width and height, from the top-left corner.

address.description: ws_ = workspace, ph_ = phone, phones = every phone allowed to reach the sending workspace, admin = relay admin, webhook:wh_ = an incoming webhook, sub_ = a subscriber (another system; only as the sender of an answer, relay-api.md Subscribers).

text.description: A text needs at least one of text, attachments, voice, location, feedback. Only the relay sets client_id, attachments, voice, location and feedback (on the text it builds for POST /v1/phone/send); a workspace message with any of them is refused (422 invalid).

general.description: true = the workspace's General conversation (no ticket; a text with general true must not carry ticket). Its only update kinds are ack and working, with reply_to = the phone's General text (the Started / Working receipt, relay-api.md). Rule (relay-api.md, General vs topics): a workspace text without ticket is General whether or not general is set; a phone text without ticket and without general is a pending new topic until an ack with reply_to = its id names the ticket. The relay never rewrites stored texts.

speak.description: Workspace texts only: worth hearing. The phone may fetch audio for it (GET /v1/phone/speech/<message id>). Spoken text = summary if set, else text (relay-api.md, Speech).

attachments.description: Phone uploads (POST /v1/phone/blobs) sent with this text. The receiving workspace may read each blob with GET /v1/blobs/<blob_id>.

kind.description: As the phone says, unchecked; a display hint only.

name.description: As the phone says, unchecked. The workspace cleans it before using it as a file name (no / or \, no leading dots, no control characters).

mime.description: As the phone says, unchecked (the relay serves every blob as application/octet-stream); a hint only, never trusted.

voice.description: The text is a voice memo: the recording (a phone upload) and what was said. The agent works from transcript; text, if set, is what the person typed next to it.

transcript.description: Empty when nothing could be transcribed.

lang_source.description: detected = by the transcriber; setting = the phone's language setting (Swiss German); corrected = the person picked it in the long-press menu.

location.description: A current location, sent once (not live).

kind.description: What this text says about the ticket's work. The relay pushes only result, question, failure and stopped; the others are stored and listed, never pushed (relay-api.md, Push). An ack or working text about a phone text carries reply_to = that phone text's id (the phone shows it as Started); the ack that starts a new topic carries the new ticket (and key).

title.description: Optional short ticket title for the phone. Same character rule as the PATCH /v1/me description (relay-api.md): one line, NFC, only letters, marks, numbers, punctuation, symbols and spaces (Unicode L, M, N, P, S, Zs), not only spaces, no control/format/line/paragraph separators, no Default_Ignorable_Code_Point characters, at most 2 combining marks in a row. The relay refuses a text that breaks it (422 invalid); NFC is checked by the relay.

update.description: Optional. A work update about the message's ticket. Old clients ignore it and show the text as before.

ticket_view.description: Optional, only next to body.update: a snapshot of the ticket for the phone's ticket chat (title, tasks, the last history lines, proof and links). Written by the sending workspace; the relay stores it with the text, never interprets it, and refuses a text whose ticket_view is over 16384 bytes as compact UTF-8 JSON (422 invalid). The newest one of a ticket wins. Plain text everywhere, never HTML; secrets are removed by the workspace before sending.

agent.description: Optional. The agent working on it now or last, as a display name (e.g. Claude).

running.description: An agent runs on the ticket now (the phone says "Goes in after this step"), else "Saved for the next run".

history_tail.description: The ticket's last history lines (at most 30), oldest first, in plain words.

who.description: Display name: the person's name or the agent's (e.g. Claude).

attachments.description: Newest first. image/file: proof files the agent marked as result or check, uploaded with POST /v1/blobs (fetched by the phone with GET /v1/phone/blobs/<blob_id>). link: proof URLs and ticket links (ticket links carry label, icon, mono and status when known). html: a published page or app (the phone opens it in its viewer). pr / commit: a pull request or a commit (title, url, status). Every url kind (link, html, pr, commit) needs url and no blob_id; image/file need blob_id, name, size and no url. id + rev name the artifact for feedback (body.feedback).

id.description: Stable per artifact across revisions: a_ + the first 12 hex characters of sha256("<source>\n<ref>") (UTF-8), where source/ref = the evidence type and ref, or "link" and the url for ticket links (vectors/phone-v3-v1.json, artifact_ids). Optional for older workspaces; feedback needs it.

rev.description: This revision of the artifact: the blob's sha256 for image/file, the commit sha for commit and pr (head), the publish id or deploy rev for html, else any short word that changes when the content changes.

label.description: Optional, url kinds only: what the link is ("GitHub · Pull request", "Figma", "Link"), from workspace/src/orch/links.py.

icon.description: Optional, url kinds only: the site or link-type icon key (github, figma, youtube, link, ...); an unknown key shows the mono tile.

mono.description: Optional, url kinds only: the letters on the tile (GH, Fg).

status.description: Optional, url kinds only: the add-on's status of the link (open, merged, unlisted); for pr the PR state (open, draft, merged, closed).

file.description: The file is uploaded first (POST /v1/blobs), stored encrypted at rest on the relay, fetched with GET /v1/blobs/<blob_id>.

title.description: Ticket title, for the phone card

previews.description: Optional: option -> the ticket_view attachment id the phone shows next to that option (A/B choices, approve with a preview). Keys are options of this question; others are ignored.

scope.description: Optional, permission questions (options Once / Always / No): what Always covers, in plain words, e.g. "sending to anna@pilatus.ch". The phone shows "Always allow <scope>".

client_id.description: Set by the relay on phone answers (POST /v1/phone/answer).

delegate.description: Hand over a new task. The receiver makes a ticket from it, but only with an allow (once or permanent).

allow_token.description: From an earlier permanent allow. Without it the receiver asks its person first.

start.description: Start an agent now on the receiver, for a named task (key). Needs an allow, like delegate.

key.description: Task name, e.g. weekly-report. A permanent allow is bound to (sender, key).

text.description: What to do. Becomes the start of the agent prompt, marked as untrusted.

allow.description: Sent by the receiver back to the asker (reply_to = the delegate/start message). once: only that message runs. permanent: later messages with this token and the same kind (+ key for start) run without asking.

refresh-hint.description: Only a hint. The workspace then runs `orch relay refresh`, which fetches from the admin-owned endpoint.

headers.description: Only X-GitHub-Event, X-GitHub-Delivery, User-Agent and X-Orch-* are kept.

payload.description: Raw request body as text (max 1 MB).
